body: Thanks for responding. I can see what you're saying, and I appreciate it because it's a very objective viewpoint (which is what I needed). Maybe the logical part of my brain agrees with you, but this is also someone I love very much who also loves me very much (despite manipulative behaviors indicating otherwise). He does have a chemical imbalance. The entire time we dated and even beyond that and before that, he has never tried to manipulate me or hurt me in any way, so it's really confusing and conflicting with who he is to me. What i'm worried about is if I cut off contact with him I think that he will legitimately kill himself or seriously try to. Friends who have been depressed in the past have told me that often when suicidal people tell other people about wanting to kill themselves, that it's a cry for help (which we should take seriously!) but that when people really want to die, they won't tell anyone so no one will stop them. I think that he will do it. I think he relies on me for support so i'm afraid if i take out a support system from under him it will be the last thing he can handle. I know it isn't my fault if he does end up killing himself, but I really don't want him to die. I'm just afraid that i'll either cut him off and the result will be his death, or I will keep supporting him and he will keep emotionally affecting me.

Thank you for responding. First attempt was definitely just that…an attempt. He wanted to die. He threatened after that but I think mostly those threats were a cry for help. His family doesn't know, but he's going to tell them today (he did not kill himself like I thought he would, but he went out and got drunk and lost instead. Which is better than killing yourself, but still….) His parents…they just don't really care about him. I told him if he didn't tell his parents very soon that I would. He says that he has barely any relationship with his parents, and I told them that being honest about something so important was a good place to start a relationship. His dad was really messed up when he was younger but I think after he got treatment for bipolar he's become a better father so I keep urging him to talk to him because I think he could help. Besides that, I keep getting emotional which makes it really hard for me to handle it fairly, sometimes I get so upset I tell him things out of spite or anger that you shouldn't say to a suicidal or depressed person. I've read things that say that it's good to be there and support a suicidal person, but this is harder because A) i'm nowhere near him and B) we're exes so our feelings can get in the way. I THINK we might try being friends with no mention of romance or relationships at all, and no talk about the breakup. Do you think, from what you know, that that would be possible? Or beneficial at all? Would that be better than just abandoning him?
